description: Builds and configures the Express app: CORS, JSON body parsing, morgan logging, static serving of /screenshots, /baselines, and /branding, plus a hardcoded /api/ai-automation/status stub and a large inline POST /api/generate-playwright-code handler that launches Playwright Chromium, walks the DOM to find named page sections (header/nav/hero/content/forms/footer), screenshots each section, and calls autoDiscoverAndGenerateSteps to compile an AI-generated manual test-step matrix. Mounts the main /api router and error-handling middleware.
exports: app (default export, the Express application instance)

description: Central configuration object loaded from environment variables via dotenv: server port/env, crawler limits, viewport definitions, Lighthouse categories, accessibility standards, visual-regression diff threshold, cross-browser browser list, storage directory paths, AI provider settings (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini), email provider settings (Gmail/Outlook/Resend), and GitHub integration settings (token, repo, base branch, workflow).

HTTP handlers for the Phase 3 AI Automation API: running the prioritize/RCA/fix pipeline (getStatus/run), opening a PR (createPr), running the CI/CD gate (cicd), merging a PR after review-gate checks (merge), analyzing a pasted issue into a PR (analyzeIssue), resolving an issue's source file/line without running the full pipeline (locate), capturing/serving an annotated screenshot of an issue (annotatedScreenshot), re-checking whether an issue is actually fixed (verify), and reviewing a pasted code snippet (reviewCode). Delegates all real logic to aiAutomation.service.js and codeReview.service.js.

GET /api/analytics handler: reads all tests, buckets them by day within a `days` window to build score/pass-fail/issue-severity trend series, computes the top 10 most-scanned domains with average scores, and computes overall/last-7-day/prev-7-day average score summaries with a percent delta.

Handles authentication endpoints: register/login with hashed passwords and signed tokens, forgot/reset-password using a random SHA-256-hashed token with a 30-minute TTL (dev builds return the raw token in the response since no email is wired for it), fetching the current user (me), and accepting a pending team invite to activate a stub account and sign in.

GET/PUT handlers for white-label branding config (primary color, header/footer text and font sizes, logo dimensions and image). Update is restricted to the workspace owner (earliest-created user) or an admin, and accepts a base64 data-URI logo which it decodes and writes to storage/branding.

Serves the static device catalog (getDevices) and handles a one-shot device render request (render), delegating the actual Playwright rendering to deviceLab.service.js and returning its screenshot URL/metadata.

CRUD and control endpoints for continuous-monitoring records: list, create (validates URL, builds a Monitor via the model), update (frequency/enabled/alertOnCritical/modules/name patch), remove, trigger an immediate scan (runNow, via monitorScheduler.service), and fetch a monitor's run history from the tests repository.
GET /api/pipeline handler returning the currently queued/running scans (id, name, url, status, progress, currentStage, startedAt) plus the queue's active/pending counts, for a live pipeline widget.

CRUD and activation endpoints for Custom Testing Policies (per-score min/max acceptance ranges): list, create, update (merges partial scoreRanges patches per key), remove, and setActive (marks one policy active, deactivating others).
GET /api/stats handler computing dashboard summary numbers from all tests: total/passed/failed/running counts, average score of completed tests, and open-issue counts broken down by severity.

Team management endpoints for this single-tenant app, where 'the team' is derived from all registered users gated by teamStatus and the earliest-created user is treated as the owner: listMembers (with computed role and per-user test activity), invite (adds an existing user directly or creates a pending token-based invite and emails a link, with a dev-only fallback link when email isn't configured), updateRole, and remove (deletes pending invites outright, otherwise clears teamStatus). Owner/admin-gated for mutating actions; the owner itself can't be role-changed or removed.

Core scan/test CRUD and issue-ticketing endpoints: create (validates URL and modules, builds a Test via the model, persists it, and enqueues the scan), list (status/search filters), getOne, remove, rerun (resets status to queued and re-enqueues), and per-issue operations getIssues, updateIssue (resolved flag / assignee list, filtered against real user ids), addIssueComment, all backed by tests.repository.js.

Builds the full device picker catalog used by Device Lab: every relevant Playwright built-in device descriptor (real UA/viewport/DPR/touch specs) grouped by category/OS, plus hand-built CUSTOM_DEVICES for brands/tiers Playwright doesn't ship descriptors for (Samsung A/M series, Xiaomi, OnePlus, OPPO, vivo, Motorola, Huawei, etc.) and a generated WINDOWS_CUSTOM_DEVICES matrix (Windows version x browser, with historically-accurate UA strings and real rendering engines mapped per browser). Exposes the combined list and a lookup helper.
Express route guard that reads the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, verifies it via utils/token.js, and attaches the decoded payload to req.user, or responds 401 if missing/invalid.

Standard Express error-handling middleware: notFound returns a 404 JSON body for unmatched routes, errorHandler logs the error and returns a JSON body with the error's status (default 500) and message.

Factory for a continuous-monitoring 'Monitor' record: url, name, frequency (hourly/daily/weekly, mapped to ms via FREQUENCY_MS), the QA modules to run (defaults to all Phase 2 modules if none given), alert-on-critical flag, enabled state, and scheduling bookkeeping fields (nextRunAt, lastRunAt, lastTestId, lastRunHadCriticalIssues, lastRunReconciled).

Factory for a Custom Testing Policy record: a min-max acceptable range for each of five scan scores (overallScore, performance, accessibility, seo, bestPractices), defaulting to a fully permissive 0-100 range for any key not explicitly configured. Only one policy can be `active` at a time.

Factory for a 'Test' (single QA scan run) record shape: identity/status/progress fields, Lighthouse-style scores and Core Web Vitals metrics, Phase 1 fields (pagesScanned, issues, brokenLinks, consoleErrors, screenshots), and Phase 2 fields that stay empty unless the corresponding module was selected (accessibility, seo, visualRegression, crossBrowser, performanceBenchmark, policyResult), plus the run's options (maxPages, maxDepth, device, modules, policyId).

Single-object (not array-based) JSON file persistence for the app's one branding config, stored at backend/data/branding.json, with hardcoded DEFAULTS merged in on read and an updatedAt timestamp set on write.
Thin CRUD wrapper around a JsonStore('monitors.json') for monitor records, returning them newest-first from list().

CRUD wrapper around a JsonStore('policies.json') for policy records, with a normalize() step that back-fills the scoreRanges field (from legacy scoreTiers/thresholds shapes) so every reader can rely on it being present; also provides getActive() and setActive() (which deactivates any other currently-active policy).
CRUD wrapper around a JsonStore('tests.json') for test/scan records, with list() supporting status and free-text (url/name) search filters and returning results newest-first.

CRUD wrapper around a JsonStore('users.json') for user accounts, including sanitize() (strips password/reset/invite token fields before returning a user to the client), createInvite() (a stub account with no password, teamStatus 'invited'), and lookups by email/reset-token-hash/invite-token-hash.
Registers GET / (protected) to analytics.controller.get.
Registers the auth endpoints: POST /register, /login, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /accept-invite (all public), and GET /me (protected).
Registers GET / (public) and PUT / (protected) to branding.controller.
Registers GET /devices and POST /render to deviceLab.controller (both public/unauthenticated).

Top-level API router that mounts every feature router under /api (auth, tests, team, policies, branding, monitors, analytics, device-lab), wires the flat /stats and /pipeline endpoints, registers the full set of /ai-automation/* endpoints directly, and exposes GET /health.
Registers monitor CRUD + control endpoints (list, create, update, delete, run-now, history), all behind the protect middleware.
Registers policy CRUD + activate endpoints, all behind the protect middleware.
Registers team member endpoints (list, invite, update role, remove), all behind the protect middleware.
Registers scan/test endpoints: create/rerun/delete/issue mutations behind protect, list/getOne/getIssues left public for read access.

Injects axe-core into an already-rendered Puppeteer page and runs a WCAG audit (categories from config.accessibility.standards), mapping raw axe rule IDs to a fixed set of readable category labels and capturing real locator/snippet info for the first few violating nodes per rule. Also runs the supplemental accessibilityCustomChecks.js checks and merges their results in with axe's.

In-page (page.evaluate) checks for accessibility gaps axe-core doesn't reliably cover: Missing Focus Indicator (focuses each focusable element and diffs computed outline/box-shadow), Broken ARIA References (id-reference attributes like aria-labelledby pointing at nonexistent ids), Small Touch Targets (interactive elements under 24x24 CSS px), Live Region (aria-live) Issues (invalid aria-live/aria-atomic values), and Keyboard Navigation Issues (pseudo-interactive elements with no tabindex). Returns findings shaped like axe violations so issueDetector.service.js can treat them identically.

Manages a single shared, lazily-launched headless Puppeteer Chromium instance used across the Phase 1/2 scan pipeline (screenshots, console errors, accessibility, SEO), auto-relaunching if the previous instance died, plus a closeBrowser() used on graceful shutdown.

Captures a real screenshot of the page an issue was found on for the 'Affected Component' view: if the issue has a still-present selector, highlights and tightly crops around that element; otherwise falls back to a full-page screenshot. Caches results to disk per testId/issueId so repeat views don't re-render the page, and returns { available:false } (never a placeholder) when there's no URL or the capture fails.
Navigates to a URL with Puppeteer and captures browser console errors/warnings, uncaught page exceptions, and failed network requests during load.

Breadth-first same-origin link crawl starting from a URL, using plain axios + cheerio (no browser) for fast link discovery up to configured max pages/depth, collecting each visited page's status code plus a separate set of discovered external links (checked for brokenness elsewhere by linkChecker.service.js).

Loads a URL in each configured Playwright browser engine (chromium/firefox/webkit) using domcontentloaded (not networkidle, to avoid timeouts on sites with persistent network activity) and reports per-browser ok/status/load-time/console-errors, or a clear 'Playwright not installed' result set if the playwright package can't be required.

One-shot Device Lab renderer: launches a real Playwright browser engine (chosen from the device's default or an override) with a device descriptor from deviceCatalog.js applied, navigates to a URL, takes a viewport screenshot, and returns its URL plus device/orientation/status/timing metadata. Used by the /render REST endpoint (as opposed to the live socket session in deviceLabSession.service.js).

Backs the real-time, interactive Device Lab: manages one live Playwright page per connected socket (with a shared, warm browser-process pool per engine so device switches don't relaunch a fresh browser each time), streams JPEG screenshots on load/idle/action, and relays devtools-style data over the socket — console messages, network request/response/failure events, DOM content, computed-style/box-model element inspection with matched CSS rules, localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies, navigation timing/paint metrics, JS heap memory, and raw source-file fetches. Also queues and throttles input actions (click/type/key/scroll/navigate/back/forward/reload) to keep the live frame in sync without lag.

Finds the real, on-disk source file and exact literal snippet that a scan-observed issue actually lives in, inside a repo already matched by repoRegistry.service.js — grounding AI-generated fixes in real code instead of guessing. Walks and caches a repo's candidate source files, then tries exact snippet matching, whitespace-insensitive matching, class-list matching (handles JSX className vs rendered class, including truncated Lighthouse snippets), attribute-anchored matching (src/href), Next.js `metadata` export detection for document-level SEO issues, and direct source-location resolution for console errors. Returns null (never a fuzzy guess) when no confident match exists.

Dedicated Google Gemini client used specifically for AI-assisted source-file location (large-context 'which of these many files' problem), independent of the main AI_PROVIDER switch in llm.service.js. Lazily constructs the SDK client only if GEMINI_API_KEY is set, and provides a JSON-completion call with one automatic retry on failure/unparseable output; returns null (never throws) so callers fall back to the existing llm.service path.

Minimal native-fetch GitHub REST client used to turn a QA remediation into a real pull request and drive CI/CD via GitHub Actions. Auto-resolves the token (from the OS git credential store, or GITHUB_TOKEN) and target repo (from `git remote get-url origin`, or GITHUB_REPO) with zero manual setup. Provides ensureBranch/openOrFindPR, applyRemediation (patches a real file on GitHub only if its current content still contains the expected original snippet — else throws FileDriftedError; refuses with NoCodeChangeError if there's no real patch), workflow dispatch/run polling, an app-level PR review-decision gate (approve/changes-requested tally, standing in for GitHub's native required-review protection on free-tier private repos), merge state lookup, and merging.

Converts raw scan findings (broken links, console errors, Lighthouse failing audits, accessibility violations, SEO checks, visual-regression diffs, cross-browser failures) into a unified Issue list with severity, a bug-tracker-style issueType classification (UI/API/Accessibility/CSS/Functional/SEO/Performance/Security, keyword-classified for the multi-purpose 'lighthouse' category), and real observed locator/snippet data where available. buildIssuesAndScore combines everything and computes the overall 0-100 score as the average of the four Lighthouse category scores.

Runs a Lighthouse audit against a URL via chrome-launcher, extracting per-category scores (performance/accessibility/seo/bestPractices), Core Web Vitals metrics, the worst 20 failing audits (cross-referencing companion 'element' diagnostic audits for LCP/CLS to attach a real selector/snippet where possible), and real pass/fail/total counts across every scoreable audit (used for the CI/CD summary).

Concurrency-limited (p-limit) HEAD (falling back to GET on 4xx/5xx, since some servers mishandle HEAD) check of a list of URLs, returning only the ones that are broken (4xx/5xx or a network/timeout error).

Provider-agnostic LLM client for the AI Automation engine, supporting Anthropic and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Groq, Together, Ollama, LM Studio) via native fetch only. isEnabled() reflects whether the configured provider has an API key; complete()/completeJSON() never throw — they return null on any failure so every caller can fall back to deterministic logic. Also provides sanitizeCode() to strip code-fence wrappers and stray prose lines from LLM-returned code.

Email sending abstraction over three interchangeable providers — Gmail SMTP, Outlook/Microsoft SMTP (both via nodemailer), and Resend's REST API (via fetch) — auto-selected by which is configured (or forced via EMAIL_PROVIDER). send() logs and reports failure if nothing is configured, rather than throwing. Provides templated helpers for team-invite and team-added-notification emails.

Continuous-monitoring scheduler: a 60-second tick checks for enabled monitors whose nextRunAt is due, triggers a new scan (creating a Test record and enqueuing it) for each, reschedules nextRunAt by the monitor's frequency, and separately reconciles finished monitor runs to flag lastRunHadCriticalIssues. startScheduler() runs the tick immediately at boot (to catch up on anything overdue) and then on the interval.
Compares the current scan's Core Web Vitals metrics against the most recent previous completed run for the same URL, computing a per-metric delta (negative = faster/better) for trend display.

In-process concurrency-limited (p-limit, default 2 via SCAN_CONCURRENCY) scan queue: enqueueScan schedules runScan(testId) from scanEngine.service.js, with pendingCount/activeCount exposed for the pipeline endpoint.

Multi-repo detection: figures out which local git repo on disk a scanned URL actually belongs to, so PR generation targets the right project. Discovers candidate repos from VS Code's own crash-recovery workspace-folder record plus fixed fallback roots, then matches a URL by hostname (package.json homepage or SITE_URL-style env keys), by which repo's dev server process is actually listening on the URL's port right now (via netstat + CIM process command-line lookup, Windows-only), by URL path segment vs. folder name, or by a static dev-port guess from package.json scripts — reporting 'unmatched'/'ambiguous_*' rather than ever silently guessing a wrong repo.

Captures full-page Puppeteer screenshots of a URL at each configured viewport (mobile/tablet/desktop), saving them under storage/screenshots/<testId>/ for dashboard previews and as the basis for visual-regression comparisons.

Orchestrates the full QA scan pipeline for a Test record: Phase 1 (always runs) crawl, broken-link check, responsive screenshots, console-error capture, Lighthouse audit; Phase 2 (opt-in per test.options.modules) accessibility, SEO, visual regression, cross-browser, and performance-benchmark checks. Updates progress/currentStage on the test as each stage runs, aggregates everything into a scored issue list via issueDetector.service.js, evaluates the test against its chosen (or the active) score-range policy, writes a full JSON report to storage/reports/<testId>.json, and persists final results back to the test record.

Renders a URL via the shared Puppeteer browser (to survive bot-protection that a raw HTTP GET would trip) and runs cheerio-based on-page SEO checks: title length, meta description length, single-h1 presence, image alt-text coverage, canonical link, viewport meta tag, noindex robots meta, Open Graph tags, and JSON-LD structured data — each check carries a pass/fail message and, on failure, the relevant real HTML snippet. Produces a 0-100 score from the pass ratio.

A standalone, heavily-annotated reference implementation of visual regression (Playwright capture + pixelmatch diff, stabilization CSS to kill animations, baseline-per-(url,viewport) identity, loopback-target guard, size-mismatch handling, baseline approval) with example Express routes left commented out at the bottom. Not required or mounted anywhere in the app — scanEngine.service.js uses services/visualRegression.service.js instead, so this file is dead/unused legacy code, not part of the live request pipeline.

The visual-regression implementation actually wired into the scan pipeline (required by scanEngine.service.js). Compares each of the current run's already-captured responsive screenshots against a stored per-URL/per-viewport baseline (storage/baselines/<urlHash>/<viewport>.png) using pixelmatch; the first scan for a URL establishes the baseline, later scans are flagged 'significant' if the diff percentage exceeds config.visualRegression.diffThresholdPercent, with a diff image written out when pixels differ.

AI Code Review: given a pasted code snippet, either asks the configured LLM (via llm.service.js) for a structured JSON review (summary, line-referenced issues with severity/category, and a fully corrected version of the snippet) or, if no AI provider is configured, falls back to cheap regex-based heuristics (hardcoded hex colors, hardcoded px values on layout properties, suspicious literal secrets/URLs/large numbers) that flag issues without claiming an auto-fix (correctedCode stays null).

The Phase 3 AI Automation engine: turns a completed scan's real issues into prioritization (severity + category-weighted scoring, favoring systemic/high-frequency categories), root-cause analysis (honest, evidence-based location/confidence per issue category — never fabricating a source file it can't know), suggested fixes (grounded, real-repo-file patches via fileLocator.service.js when a repo can be matched and the fix pattern is safe to auto-apply e.g. missing alt/aria-label/lang/tabindex/canonical, LLM-tailored when enabled and its output is verified to echo the real original snippet, deterministic templates otherwise), a CI/CD quality-gate summary built from real scan-derived pass/fail counts, and PR creation/merging against the correct local repo (auto-matched via repoRegistry.service.js) with a real-file-drift check before patching and an app-level review-approval gate before merge. Also supports analyzing a pasted issue (recovering it from a copied testId/issueId reference or free-text parsing) into the same pipeline, verifying whether a specific issue is actually still failing by re-running its underlying check, capturing an annotated screenshot of an issue's element, and self-healing issue-resolved state when a PR is merged outside the app.

Registers the /device-lab Socket.IO namespace and wires each socket event (start, input, inspect-dom, inspect-at, inspect-storage, inspect-performance, inspect-memory, fetch-source, stop, disconnect) straight through to the corresponding deviceLabSession.service.js function, acknowledging start/failure via the socket.io ack callback.

Maps axe-core's ~50 granular rule IDs down to a fixed set of 20 readable accessibility category labels (e.g. 'aria-command-name' and 'select-name' both become 'Missing Accessible Name') used as issue titles; unmapped rule IDs fall back to axe's own help text rather than being dropped.

Small shared wrapper around the local `git` binary (via child_process execFileSync): runs arbitrary git commands in a given cwd, pulls a host's credential from the OS git credential helper (Git Credential Manager/Keychain/libsecret), and parses/resolves a repo's 'owner/repo' GitHub slug from its origin remote URL. Used by both github.service.js and repoRegistry.service.js.

Minimal file-backed JSON array store class (backend/data/<fileName>, shape { items: [] }) providing getAll/getById/insert/update/remove, with a naive write-lock promise chain so concurrent writes to the same file don't clobber each other. The persistence layer behind every repository in this app.
Tiny ANSI-colored console logger with info/success/warn/error levels, each prefixed with an ISO timestamp and a tag.
Password hashing/verification using Node's built-in crypto.scrypt (no external dependency), storing 'salt:hash' and comparing with a constant-time buffer comparison.

Standalone 'Auto-Pilot' E2E job processor (contains Hindi/English mixed comments): scans a target URL's HTML with Playwright, calls testGenerator.js to have Claude generate interactive test steps, runs them via a separate Playwright test spec (dynamicEngine.spec.ts) through npx, captures a failure screenshot artifact on error, and reports a final status object through an updateGlobalStore callback. Not wired into the main scan pipeline (scanEngine.service.js/queue.service.js is the actual live queue) — appears to be an alternate/earlier automation path.

Calls the Anthropic API directly (via @anthropic-ai/sdk, independent of llm.service.js's provider abstraction) with a detailed prompt instructing it to write manual QA test cases in a specific professional style (multi-step user journeys grounded only in real HTML content per page section), then flattens the returned JSON test cases into individual step rows matching a spreadsheet-style convention (Work Item Type/Title only on each case's first row). Used by both app.js's /api/generate-playwright-code endpoint and utils/queueProcessor.js.

Minimal JWT-style signed token implementation using built-in crypto HMAC-SHA256 (no jsonwebtoken dependency): sign() base64url-encodes a payload with iat/exp and appends an HMAC signature; verify() checks the signature with a constant-time comparison and rejects expired tokens. Uses JWT_SECRET from env, warning loudly and falling back to an insecure dev secret if unset.

Backend npm package manifest: declares the Express 5 / Puppeteer / Playwright / Lighthouse / axe-core / cheerio / nodemailer / socket.io / pixelmatch dependency set, `npm start` (node server.js) and `npm run dev` (nodemon) scripts, and requires Node >=18.

The real process entry point: wraps app.js's Express app in an http.Server, attaches a Socket.IO server and registers the device-lab namespace (sockets/deviceLab.socket.js), injects a second (largely redundant/older-style) POST /api/generate-playwright-code handler directly on the app instance that scans a page with Playwright and compiles a literal Playwright test-spec string via testGenerator.js, starts listening on config.port, starts the monitor scheduler, and handles graceful shutdown (closing the shared Puppeteer browser) on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

Standalone diagnostic script: launches headless Chromium via Playwright, prints its version on success, or an error plus a 'run npx playwright install chromium' hint on failure. Not required by any other module — a manual troubleshooting utility.

Template environment file documenting every optional/required backend env var: server port/env, crawler tuning, scan concurrency, and the fully-optional Phase 3 AI Automation settings (AI_PROVIDER plus Anthropic/OpenAI keys, and GitHub token/repo/base-branch/workflow for real PR + Actions integration), with comments explaining that the app degrades gracefully (deterministic rules, honest 'not connected' states) when any of these are unset.

Project README describing the Phase 1 MVP feature set (crawling, responsive screenshots, broken-link detection, Lighthouse, console-error detection, scored QA reports), setup instructions, a walkthrough of how a scan request flows through the queue/scanEngine pipeline into a stored JSON report, a REST API reference for the core tests/stats/pipeline endpoints, the project's directory structure, notes on future phases, and instructions for pointing the existing Next.js frontend at this backend.
